rationale: Review started 2026-11-10T06:54:52Z and ended 2026-11-10T07:05:36Z (UTC). I re-hashed jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9680.txt and EO_9285.recheck.txt (both match their recorded hashes, as do all source fingerprints), confirmed the spans, and read EO 9680 (11 FR 735, signed January 17, 1946) in full, confirming its identity. Its first operative paragraph abolishes the United States of America Typhus Commission, created by EO 9285 (which ACTOR_TEXT:EO:9285 correctly identifies and which no held text ended earlier), 'as of June 30, 1946', a self-executing own-terms end; but its second operative paragraph directs that the liquidation of the Commission's affairs and the disposition of its records, scientific data and material 'shall be accomplished under the supervision and direction of the Secretary of War', a one-time command with no stated end. The rationale gives no evidence or reason that this liquidation command was performed or ended, and I found none in held sources: a cruden number search for EO 9680 and a literal search for 'Typhus Commission' found no later instrument, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches had 0 hits. Under the 2026-10-28 ruling, exhaustion by performance needs evidence and an event not shown to have happened leaves the order open for that question; by analogy the 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling does not treat a functionally spent task as the order's end. The selected basis does not carry an ending either: the CLAUSES:EO:9680#whole span (chars 1766-2131) holds the liquidation paragraph and only the '1946.' tail of the abolition sentence, and ACTOR_TEXT:EO:9285 is the creating order, included, as the rationale says, only because it is the dossier's sole actor record; disclosing that does not make it an ending basis. Rejected: the abolition of the Commission on June 30, 1946 is supported, but a whole-order NO through 2026-10-14 is not established until the liquidation direction's performance or end is shown from held sources.
